findings.area: GET /gamification/stats data integrity (ADR-1 consequence, P4/P5, Missions+Me screens)
findings.finding: The plan lists `/gamification/stats` as a 'REAL, verified' backend contract and wires it as the canonical Missions/Me stats source (ADR-1's consequence line, P4's use-gamification hook, P5's gamification adapter). I traced the actual handler: `server/src/routes/gamification.routes.ts` reads `const userId = req.user!.id` (lines 24, 42, 75, 98, 116, 134) but `IJwtPayload` (server/src/types/index.ts:33-38) and every place it is constructed (auth.middleware.ts loadAuthenticatedUser, generateTokens call sites) only ever set `.userId`, never `.id`. So `req.user!.id` is always `undefined` on every authenticated request. `gamificationService.getUserStats(undefined)` runs `WHERE id = $1` with a null-coerced param (pg treats `undefined == null`), always returns zero rows, and the service's documented 'user not found, returning default stats' fallback fires (server/src/services/gamification.service.ts:441-452) for every user, not just fresh ones. The batch's own evidence used a freshly seeded account with genuinely 0 XP, so the fixture cannot distinguish 'honest fresh-account zero' from 'this confirmed bug' - but the code proves it's the latter for any real, XP-having user too. The plan already knows about the `.id`/`.userId` inconsistency (OQ-6) but treats it as a soft 'verify before BIOS-008' item, while this exact batch ships UI (Missions, Me) that will silently display Level 1 / 0 XP / 0 streak for every real user, indefinitely, looking like real data rather than an honest-null - directly undermining the batch's own stated thesis. It also likely produces a visible cross-tab inconsistency: Today's `momentum.xp/streak/level` comes from `overview/dashboard`, whose controller resolves `userId` correctly via `req.user?.userId` (per scope-map), so Today may show correct XP/streak while Missions/Me show 0 for the same user.
findings.failure_scenario: A real user with e.g. Level 5 / 1200 XP / 7-day streak opens the Missions or Me tab after this batch ships; the screen reads `/gamification/stats`, gets the all-zero fallback (server-side bug, not client fabrication), and displays 'Level 1, 0 XP, 0-day streak' as if it were real - while the Today tab (sourced from `overview/dashboard`) may correctly show their real streak/XP, producing a visibly self-contradictory app.
findings.recommendation: Before treating `/gamification/stats` as a trustworthy adapter source for this batch: (a) verify with a non-fresh seeded account that has real XP/streak whether the endpoint actually returns nonzero data, and (b) either land the one-line backend fix (`req.user!.id` -> `req.user!.userId` in gamification.routes.ts) as part of this batch, or add an explicit waiver + a defensive check in the adapter until the backend bug is fixed. Do not ship Missions/Me trusting this endpoint silently.

findings.area: ADR-5 / Packet P6 - Cia chat entitlement & credit-consumption contract is incomplete
findings.finding: The live (non-onboarding) `/ai-coach/chat` call is gated by two middlewares in sequence: `requireFeature('ai.coach.message')` (402 `FEATURE_DISABLED`, which the plan does cover) AND `consumeCredits('ai.coach.message')` (server/src/middlewares/entitlement.middleware.ts:330-386). The plan's ADR-5 and P6 packet only mention the `FEATURE_DISABLED` code. `consumeCredits` independently requires an `Idempotency-Key` request header - if missing and enforcement is active, it throws `400 { code: 'MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY' }` (lines 340-348); if credits are exhausted it throws `402 { code: 'CREDITS_EXHAUSTED' }` (lines 371-385), a distinct case from feature-gating implying different UX. None of this is embedded in the P6 packet, and GLM builds only from the packet text. Today this is masked because `env.entitlement.mode` defaults to `'shadow'` (server/src/config/env.config.ts:388-397, confirmed default), so missing-header and exhausted-credit denials are currently logged, not blocked. But the code comment explicitly says the intended rollout is to flip to `'enforce-new'` once the ledger has run clean - a near-term, planned event, not a hypothetical.
findings.failure_scenario: Once entitlement enforcement flips from shadow to enforce-new/enforce-all, every live-tab Cia message sent by the built mobile client (which never sends `Idempotency-Key`) starts failing with 400 `MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`; separately, a user who runs out of credits gets a `CREDITS_EXHAUSTED` 402 that the plan's single-code gated-state handling will mishandle or mislabel as a plan-upgrade prompt when it's actually a credit-balance issue.
findings.recommendation: Extend P6's embedded contract to (1) send an `Idempotency-Key` header on the live (non-onboarding) chat POST, and (2) branch the 402/400 gated-state UI on `code` (`FEATURE_DISABLED` vs `CREDITS_EXHAUSTED` vs `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` vs `MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`) with distinct, honest copy for each, not a single generic locked-feature state.

findings.area: Section 4 - packet dependency graph is internally inconsistent for P3/P4
findings.finding: The pipeline table places P3 and P4 in the same parallel stage: `Stage 1 (needs P1,P2): P3 P4`. But P4's own packet body says its target file `src/app/_layout.tsx` must 'wrap `SessionProvider` inside `QueryClientProvider`' and lists `Deps: P1, P2 (P3 for provider order)` - i.e. P4 cannot correctly complete its stated acceptance criteria without P3's `SessionProvider` already existing. The plan correctly handles the equivalent pattern elsewhere (Stage 2's table explicitly annotates 'P5 needs P4'), but the equivalent annotation is missing from Stage 1 for P4-needs-P3. If the orchestrator dispatches strictly per the stage diagram, P4 will be built in parallel with, not after, P3.
findings.failure_scenario: GLM workers for P3 and P4 run concurrently per the Stage 1 dispatch; the P4 worker, given only its own packet text, has no `SessionProvider` export to import and either invents a stub, leaves the wiring incomplete, or the orchestrator has to manually stall P4 - a process gap not reflected anywhere in the documented pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Fix the stage table to make P4 a Stage-2 packet (after P3), or explicitly annotate Stage 1 as 'P4 needs P3 for provider order' the same way Stage 2 flags the P5/P4 relationship, and adjust the orchestrator's dispatch order accordingly before Move E begins.

findings.area: ADR-3 / Packet P5 - Mission tier derivation is under-specified for the non-primary branch
findings.finding: P5's embedded mapping table gives a crisp, deterministic rule only for the primary case: `isPrimary && source==='life' -> 'life'`, `isPrimary -> 'main'`. For everything else it says only 'else by `source`/`cadence`' with no concrete lookup table. `UnifiedGoal.cadence` is documented (scope-map) as an untyped `string | null | undefined` with no enumerated values traced from the server, and `source` only distinguishes health/life/career/finance (four values) against six canon mission tiers (life/main/side/daily/weekly/group). ADR-3 explicitly claims this mapping is 'documented, deterministic, no invention' - but the actual rule for the non-primary majority of goals is left to the implementer (GLM) to invent, which is precisely the failure mode the ADR says it's avoiding.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-primary finance-source goal with `cadence: 'monthly'` (a plausible but untraced value) reaches P5's adapter; GLM has no documented rule to map it to 'side' vs 'daily' vs 'weekly' and must guess a classification rule that was never verified against real server semantics - silently reintroducing invented business logic into the honesty-focused adapter layer.
findings.recommendation: Before dispatching P5, either trace the actual `cadence` enum values emitted by the goals-aggregator service for each source table and write out the full source x cadence -> tier lookup table explicitly, or fall back non-primary goals to a single conservative tier (e.g. always 'side') documented as a known simplification rather than an inferred rule.

findings.finding: The stored-session schema adds required fields (`refreshToken` now required, new `accessTokenExpiresAt`, `schemaVersion:1`) under the unchanged key `balencia.mobile.session.v1`. No migration/validation step is specified for a session written by the pre-batch shell (optional `refreshToken`, no `accessTokenExpiresAt`, no `schemaVersion`) that might still be present in SecureStore on a device that already ran the old build.
findings.failure_scenario: A simulator or a real device that previously ran the pre-BIOS-002 build has an old-shape session persisted; on the next launch after this batch ships, boot hydration reads it, `accessTokenExpiresAt` is `undefined`, and the proactive-staleness check behaves unpredictably instead of cleanly treating it as an invalid/legacy session.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit `schemaVersion` check on read: if missing or `!== 1`, treat as absent (clear + route to sign-in) rather than trusting partial old-shape data.

strengths: The verified backend contract snapshot (section 2) checks out against ground truth: every field name, nesting, and null-shape cross-checked against scope-map.json, the endpoint-sample fixtures, and the live server source (overview.ts fields, LifeAreaSummaryRow snake_case, UserGamificationStats shape, WorkoutPlan absence of score/recovery/minutes) is accurate, including the more precise claims that go beyond scope-map (e.g. DELETE_ACCOUNT_CONFIRMATION = 'DELETE MY ACCOUNT' verified byte-for-byte at server/src/validators/user.validator.ts:42).

ADR-1 (single overview/dashboard call for Today) and ADR-3's anti-fabrication mapping rules directly and correctly target the two real defects in the current shell (getFitnessDashboard's hardcoded score/recovery/weeklyMinutes formula, and GamificationStats.lifePower, which indeed does not exist server-side) - verified directly against src/services/api/pilot.ts and src/types/pilot.ts.

Scope discipline is real: ADR-6 correctly declines to widen the nav/tab structure, the 7-slice cap is respected throughout the packet decomposition, and waivers (W1-W6)/open questions are tracked explicitly rather than silently assumed away.
